subject: health
unitTitle: Nutrition, Movement, Sleep, and Performance Without Diet Culture
title: Correction and reflection: body respect and media literacy
essentialQuestion: How can understanding nutrition, movement, sleep, and performance without diet culture help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Body respect means treating bodies with dignity and supporting function, comfort, access, and care; edited images and narrow ideals are not reliable measures of health.
Check authorship, expertise, evidence, currency, uncertainty, and incentive before using a health message; confidence, popularity, and testimonials are not substitutes for support.
For body respect and media literacy, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Evaluate fictional wellness plans for adequacy, safety, evidence, and flexibility without calories, weight targets, or moralizing food.
studentTask: Compare two supplied fictional messages about body respect and media literacy. Build a four-row check for source or author, evidence, date or context, and incentive; then choose the stronger message, cite two details, and state what remains uncertain.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in body respect and media literacy; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the body respect and media literacy task using the supplied fictional or public case.
